utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You have in front of you, Admiral, a map. I just will get my copy. Do you recognise this map, Admiral Jokic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise it, but these are units of the 2nd Corps. These are not my units. What I see on the monitor that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, we're looking -- perhaps the usher may have placed it not -- if it is too difficult, then it may be easier, Admiral, to have it on the board, but I'd ask you first to look at the title of the map at the very top of it if you can, the title that is written on the map.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the working map of the command of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Is this a headquarters map, Admiral?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is a working map of the headquarters of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And covering what period, Admiral Jokic, if you can tell us, if it's indicated there. Perhaps it needs to be opened to the upper left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the 24th to the 26th of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, if that is not a comfortable way for you to assist us with this map, perhaps it would be easier to put it on the board rather than you have strain. It may require you getting up. Admiral, do you know if this map was made in the period indicated on the map?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And was this map a map that you provided or handed to the officers of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And did you connect -- did you have this map or get this map in connection with any particular reason, perhaps personal reason?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I got the original on the basis of which I had to make a copy in order to prepare my defence and to explain the course of the operation at the Dubrovnik front where I was commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What does this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before we go any further, I think we need to adjust the map so that it is facing squarely toward the Bench. In that position, it may be able to be seen by the Defence as well as the Prosecution. I think we've improved things.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Taking a general look at some of the markings on the map, in the upper right-hand corner, Admiral, there is a box. Could you please describe what is written in the box that has a -- actually some initials and a serial number? It's in the upper right hand -- in the upper top. That's it, Admiral.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Survey of the balance of forces."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Of what formation, what units?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Units of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And in the column on the left-hand side, what -- what is indicated? The first column that reads down, what is --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the left side is the artillery, the firing pieces.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I think perhaps I'm not -- I may not be clear, Admiral. Where it says -- there's a box and then there are a number of columns. The first column down. It says something about the command of the 2nd Operational Group. Can you see that, Admiral?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can see it. This is actually the composition of the command, the officers, and also all the subordinate units, the number of soldiers and the number of officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Which subordinate units, Admiral, are listed as subordinate units under the command of the 2nd Operational Group? Which ones are shown in these boxes?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Corps, the 37th corps, the 472nd Brigade, and the 9th Sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Perhaps we're looking at a different column, but if you take a look again, after the 37th Corps, what is written after the 37th Corps?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says how many officers, how many junior officers, and how many soldiers there are, and then there is the grand total.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, where you've listed the units under the command of the 2nd Operational Group, you listed the 2nd Corps, it's in blue, the 37th Corps in green. Was in pink or red below 37th Corps?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 9th VPS in red.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And that is your formation over which you had command?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And the columns indicate numbers of officers. And what does the column in blue indicate? It has a -- it's blue at the top next to "officers."

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think we're looking at the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, we are. At the top --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The blue here is junior officers and soldiers and the red stands for officers, senior officers. Yellow is the grand total.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And the green is -- did you say soldiers, soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: An overall -- an overall figure, the overall total for the 2nd Operational Group during this time period is what, Admiral? What is the overall figure?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay. Admiral, if we can look at -- emphasising the area that goes toward Dubrovnik, which should be in the lower part, and particularly the 9th VPS area, there is a legend on the left side of the map. I'd ask you to look at the legend where it has as of a particular date lines indicating what? What does the legend show us? Where it says 24, 10 --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you see here are subcolours for certain dates, the 24th, the 25th, and 26th. The whole map is in relation to the colours in relation to the specific locations of the units on the 24th, 25th, and 26th.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And does that indicate also the territories or areas held by those units or captured by the units at that -- on those dates?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I realise it is very small, but if you can indicate -- if we're looking at the blue and red line which addresses the 24th of October, can you take the pointer, please, and indicate what areas that encompasses on the 24th of October?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 24th of October, you have indication here of a line of confrontation between the 2nd Corps. It's the red line to the north and to the north-west, you have units of the 2nd Corps. To the east and to the south you have units of the 472nd Brigade and the 9th VPS. Here on this map you have a reference for the 2nd Tactical Group that had been disbanded on the 21st of October, and this is an error.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I want to focus if we can on the areas of the 472nd Brigade and on the 9th VPS. So if we can start looking at these areas that are -- that have the blue and red line. Can you just point to those, please.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here you can see the town of Dubrovnik, and along the approach roads under the blockade you can see units of the 472nd brigade, this brigade's battalions: The 1st Battalion, the 2nd Battalion, the 3rd Battalion, the 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If we can look at the map to determine both what units of the various battalions were in place, can we start first with -- toward the bottom where it says "4 472," the 4th Battalion of the 472nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This battalion was in a position that was the nearest to Dubrovnik and the Old Town, the Dubac and Brgat positions, Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can you indicate perhaps the distances of these various places you have just mentioned from Dubrovnik, and particularly from the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The nearest elevation, Zarkovica, is about 2 kilometres. Dubac is about 3 kilometres, and Brgat about 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can you assist us in pointing out on this map where the Old Town of Dubrovnik is?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are you pointing to an area that has sort of little orange dots, as it were?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can't see the dots here. Well, you can actually see them, but they're not very clear, but, yes, that's what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: For the record, to capture where the location is, it is to the right of the printed word "Dubrovnik" on the map, and it appears to be a small cluster of reddish or orange-ish dots perhaps reflecting the roof tiles. On the 24th of November, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I question what you have just said. I think it is to the north of the printed designation "Dubrovnik" rather than to the east.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not clear that we're pointing at the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have the printed designation "Dubrovnik," well away to the south-east the island of Lokrum.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: No, but above it -- if I followed the Admiral's pointer correctly, there is a small area to the east of Dubrovnik, and although very tiny. See, it is east of the word Dubrovnik and it appears to have little red dots.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be allowed to explain. It's exactly parallel to the letter K where you have the red dots at a distance from the letter K. The distance is perhaps two centimetres. That is the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Admiral, yes, and I think we now all have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, on Zarkovica, you indicated is the closest point in this area. When was -- when did Zarkovica --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: -- become -- when was it seized by forces of the two -- of the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 24th -- between the 24th and the 25th October.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are you able on this map to point out a feature known as Srdj?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the north of the Old Town at a distance of one and a half centimetres. Right to the north.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can you indicate the distance of -- of Srdj -- between Srdj and the Old Town first, and then I'll ask you about the distance between Srdj and Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between Srdj and the Old Town, the town wall, about a kilometre and a half, maybe 1.800 metres, between 1.500 and 1.800 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And between Srdj and Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between Srdj and Zarkovica, I think less than a kilometre or about a kilometre, thereabouts. Maybe a kilometre and a half.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Between the Old Town and Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two kilometres. Two something. As the crow flies, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Within the area that is shown in the red and blue lines where it says 4th Battalion of the 472nd Brigade, can you -- can you tell us what types of weaponry were at the disposal of the units of the 2nd Operational Group that were there, meaning the 4th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Battalion had the same weapons as all the other battalions establishment-wise, the same weapons as the 3rd Battalion. One mortar battery, 120-millimetres. It had 80-millimetre mortars that were part of the battery and these were usually attached to companies. Six 80-millimetre mortars altogether. It had a recoilless gun as part of the anti-armour company, four such guns, three or four launchers, Maljutkas. It had hand-held launchers, and that was that in terms of artillery.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What weapons that you have referred to belonging to this battalion were within firing range of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Old Town was within the range of all these weapons with the exception of the recoilless guns that have very small range, between a thousand and 1.500 metres in terms of their practical range. Mortars, 120 and 82, the launchers and the Maljutkas were within range of the Old Town. However, I must point out that at the time, there was no firing. The 4th Battalion was not firing on the Old Town. It is only hypothetically speaking that we can discuss these possibilities, but this battalion had been pulled out, and it did not operate. It did not fire on the Old Town while it was in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Let us look now at the area where the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade is marked. Can you first assist us with the units that belong to the 3rd Battalion? It says 1, 2, 3. What is that referring to, Admiral?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This 1, 2, 3: 1, 2 these are the brigade's battalions just across the Rijeka Dubrovacka. This is the 1st Battalion and this is the 2nd Battalion. The 3rd Battalion, in the same period of time on the 24th or the 25th was withdrawn. It was pulled out of combat because of the losses that it had suffered and because the commander had been seriously wounded. It was on account of their losses that they had been pulled out, and they reassembled in this area over here, and later it was sent to Ivanica and Trebinje. It was sent on leave, the entire 3rd Battalion. That was after the 25th. Or, rather, on the 25th they were already on leave. They had been evacuated from the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you for a moment, Admiral, and just ask you if the numbers 1, 2, 3 are referring to battalions or to smaller units. Perhaps there was either a mistranslation or perhaps we misunderstood you. What size unit, what type of unit is 1, 2, 3 referring to?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are battalions of the Trebinje Brigade. It says clearly "motorised battalions."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Right. We're not looking at the same thing. If you see on the month, Admiral, where it says 3rd Motorised Battalion, there are smaller numbers where it says 1, 2, 3. Do you see that? Where?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: That's what I was referring to, please. Can you tell us what units those are?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the companies of that same battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Somers, before you get more deeply into this issue, I think we might have the break now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It may be a very welcome break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We have been able to reduce the area on the map we're looking at sufficiently so that it should fit on the ELMO actually now. It might be a bit easier.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral Jokic, if you could turn your attention to the ELMO which is the projector next to you, which will be showing up on your screen, and use your pointer as well, to the area where the 3rd Motorised -- the 3rd Motorised Battalion of the 472nd Brigade is shown. If you can take us through those numbers 1, 2, and 3 and tell us some type of geographical name or location where the companies are, it would be helpful. For example, 1. The 1st Company of the 3rd Motorised Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st Company is in the area to the south.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I think we're losing it on the map a little bit. If we can just hold it steady. Thank you. Sorry, Admiral, could you repeat that? The 1st Company is where, please?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the south of the Vrastica rock, two centimetres to the south. This is the area covered by the 1st Motorised Company.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And the 2nd, please, the 2nd Company of the 3rd --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Company to the north of Vrastica, two centimetres where the number 2 is on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And is there a particular name associated with that area?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rijecka Glavica. That is the name of the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And the 3rd Company of the 3rd Motorised Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 3rd Company is at Grbavac. The area of Grbavac village.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can you from -- either from memory or from your own knowledge as well as whatever may be indicated on the map indicate the weapons that belong or are at the disposal of the 1st Company?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st Company had, in addition to infantry elements, 82-millimetre mortars, hand-held launchers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And the 2nd?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All three companies were the same establishment-wise, except for the 4th Anti-armour Company which had artillery weapons for support. This company is in the area where you see the guns underneath the number 3. This is the firing group.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this black elliptical shape. This is where the firing equipment is, 82-millimetre mortars, recoilless guns, and anti-armour rocket launchers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are the weapons that you've described within firing range of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was outside the firing range of the Old Town as concerns this battalion because it was in an area that was not in the combat zone. They were preparing for being sent on leave. They're not part of the combat disposition. That's why the battalion area was shown like this on the map as opposed to the 4th Battalion. This battalion is not an active participant in these operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When you say this battalion you're pointing to the 4th battalion of the 472nd, just for the record; is that right, Admiral?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the third.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Just to help us, there is a location above the words "3rd Motorised Battalion" called --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may for the sake of the transcript, the transcript says the 4th battalion and the Admiral is talking about the 3rd Battalion, and the question of my learned friend and colleague also refers to the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm talking about the 3rd Battalion. This battalion is not taking part in combat. It has been pulled out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When you say it has been pulled out, Admiral, you're talking about the dates indicated on the map; is that correct? At that stage only?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as of the 25th of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay. Are you able to indicate -- where is Uskoplje, please?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uskoplje is to the north of this writing, the 3rd MTB. That's to the north. This is an old railway station. It's a crossroads.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Looking at the 1st -- the 1st Motorised Battalion. If that's visible. If you could move your map so that we can show the 1st MTB. Okay. What geographical areas are associated with that battalion at this particular time? There are two companies, I believe, shown. If you can break down the areas associated with the companies that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This 1st Motorised Battalion was in the Golubov Kamen area to the right of the number 2 on the map, Zaplanik and Ostra Glava, the 1st Company. That's the general area. There is no detailed disposition of these battalions simply because they did not take part in the action. Therefore, this is not the whole area being shown here, only the two forward companies are being shown.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If we can take a look at what is the 2nd Motorised Battalion, the 2 MTB.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Battalion was shown in all its parts. It was in the Osojnik area, and what is shown here are the front parts the platoons and the companies in the Zaton area and just above Mokosica and Petrovo Selo it is marked exactly here the combat disposition all the platoons and companies at the rear in the Osojnik area. One can see the reserve forces, or rather, the reserve companies.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did any of the companies or platoons you referred to of the 2nd Battalion have weapons which were in range of the Old Town on this date or on these dates?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. From these positions, Osojnik and the positions of the 1st Battalion, Zaplanik, Golubov Kamen, you couldn't fire on the Old Town from those positions. First of all on account of the distance, the distances involved, and also because in between there was the rock of Srdj, and Dubrava. You could fire on the new town. You could fire on Babin Kuk, on Petka, on Lapad, the new part of town and the port of Gruz, but the Old Town could not be targeted from those positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: There are some abbreviations, smaller abbreviations on the map that maybe you can help us with. Above 2 MTB it says ODTO. Could you explain what that is, please? Yes, where your pointer is.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Trebinje Territorial Defence detachment which was used to control territory. It was not involved in combat operations. There must be a position here that is marked. However, the purpose of that detachment was to keep an eye on territory, to provide security for facilities, to stand guard and to provide support along the possible routes of operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If we move over to the right where there are names, it says 1, 2, BPVO and there is a symbol next to it. What does the name mean and what does the symbol represent, please?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the anti-aircraft defence. These are guns, 20- or 40-millimetre guns. In the combat disposition of the brigade, this unit is used for anti-aircraft defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And to which unit is this anti-aircraft defence attached?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's part of the brigade, the brigade command. It is used to provide security in this particular situation for the artillery units, for the howitzer division, 105-millimetres. It's to the right and above. That's where it's deployed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You are pointing to an area that is marked as BRA -- I think it's a G or an O. I can't see. 1?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And under, there's a line that says HAD-105. Is that what you're referring to as the howitzer division?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's the division. This is the brigade artillery group, brigade artillery group 1 minus one battery. This is the 105-millimetre howitzer division, and then you have a symbol there. These are two 105-millimetre howitzer batteries, and one or two 120-millimetre mortar batteries. That's the composition of that particular division. It is used to provide support to the brigade along the main routes of the attack, and it covers the directions along which the battalion is being used for combat, the 1st, the 2nd, and possibly the 3rd.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: As of this -- as of these dates from these positions, are the weapons within firing range of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not of the Old Town, no. This was the far end of the range of those howitzers, and their range, their practical range, is ten kilometres, at the most 15 kilometres, which means that this unit was at the far end of the range from which you could target Dubrovnik. Its purpose was to provide support to the 1st and 2nd Battalions and the 3rd Battalion for targeting Rijeka Dubrovacka and the area between Rijeka Dubrovacka and Zaton, and it could also be used for operations along the roads leading to Dubrava but not to target Dubrovnik, not from these positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, there is a marking on the map. It looks like a flag with 472 in it. What does that represent? It has a circle, a red circle and a flag. Yes, that's it. What is that, please?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the command post of the 472nd Brigade in the Talez area. The command post at that point in time was there. This was the command post from which the brigade exercised command over its units, the battalions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And is that in which municipality and in which republic, please?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Trebinje municipality, the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but you see two signs here on the map in the Talez area. One stands for the command post and there is another sign in the Ljubovo area just like the first one so it means the brigade command had two command posts or rather one that was moving from one place to another. First it was in Ljubovo then it moved to Talez.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: There is a marking on the map. It says BR it looks like POOD. It's near a circle with some additional features. Your hand is on it now actually. It's above -- it's to the right where it says 3 MTB. It says BR POOD? Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would you point it out, please, for those of us looking? It's under -- in the area where it says 472nd -- if you leave it flat, you're fine. There you go. Okay. If you could move it down. Thank you. What does that stand for, the BR --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade anti-armour detachment. The brigade anti-armour detachment. This is the symbol that denotes it, a black ellipse, and there is number one here. This is an artillery unit for anti-armour combat. Usually these are cannons, the ZIS cannons and anti-armour missiles, then hand-held mortars and weapons for anti-armour fighting that battalions have such as Osa, Zolja, et cetera. At any rate, this is the possible way of using it towards the front end, along this communication route.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did that anti-armour weaponry or among that weaponry would Maljutkas be counted as well?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If you -- could you indicate, please, what the abbreviation POP-1 is?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is anti-armour position 1. So out of this ellipse, if necessary, the artillery pieces go out to this position here, if necessary. And this is position for anti-armour fighting. And then once given orders, these weapons are moved out here, and then returned yet again depending on the need involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And the -- the presence of the anti-armour weapons, what was the purpose? Was there a -- did -- was there a Croatian armour that was of concern? Did the Croatian side have armour that you were concerned about?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not at that time. This is a classical schematic of the deployment of a brigade in an operation involving attack. Since the brigade has this anti-armour weaponry, then the commander deploys them along the axes where they may be used in order to train them since he has this within the weaponry of the brigade, but there was no military necessity, because at the time the opposite side did not have any such weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are you able to point out any tanks indicated within the 472nd Brigade on this map?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not here, because the terrain does not allow the use of tanks. So they were not there in that brigade or, rather, the 2nd Operational Group had a tank unit which was in Popovo Polje. The brigade had got a company with old World War II tanks, T-32, that were so obsolete that finally this company was split into two or three smaller groups. Later on, they were at Dubrava facing Srdj, and they were given to the 3rd Battalion. Two were dug in, and two were manoeuvering ones for self-defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Admiral. Can you indicate the most forward line as of the 20 -- for the 472nd Brigade as of the 26th of October?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most forward point was Zarkovica, here within the combat deployment of the 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And again the distance of that most forward line from Dubrovnik, the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around two or two and a half kilometres to the first walls near the Old City port. About two and a half kilometres. Two or two and a half.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: All right. Can you indicate the waters now around Dubrovnik? Who was in control of the waters at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The blockade of town from the sea was carried out by the 9th Sector, the units of the 16th Group that had four patrol boats and one gunboat. These were small boats, about 100 tonnes each, which very little weaponry. In peacetime, they were used for controlling fishing boats and defending the sea, preventing smuggling and so on. Their basic task was to act on the -- on the line Cavtat, Mljet, Kolocep, Dubrovnik Islands and in that patrol there were usually one to two boats. Their task was to stop smuggling by speedboats and other smaller, fast boats during the night which came from Metkovic and Ston via these Dubrovnik islands during the night. They came to the port of Gruz and supplied the town with weapons and other combat needs. Also, these boats intercepted or, rather, checked all the boats that came into Dubrovnik, checked all the boats that were coming from the outside, those who -- those who were allowed to enter into order to supply the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Admiral. I think that pretty well explains who was in control of the -- the coastal waters. From what you have described with the lines and the waters, would you be able to -- would you characterise the situation in the Dubrovnik area, at least as far as the city of Dubrovnik was concerned as encircled or totally blockaded?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: At this time, that is up to the 26th of October, was -- to what formation was the 472nd Motorised Brigade directly subordinated?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to the 26th of October, the 472nd Brigade was directly subordinate to the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And that was commanded by?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commanded by General Strugar.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask to move this exhibit into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P120.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: May I ask you, please, to turn your attention to tab 21. This is a document, Admiral, which is dated the 20 -- I'm sorry, one further question on the map. Do the positions which you have shown on the map depict or are -- as of the 23rd of October, would the positions of the 2nd Operational Group differ to those which you have shown on the map from, let's say the 24th to the 26th of October?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your point.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Let me rephrase it. The positions that you have shown us on the map reflect the period 24 to 26 October. Would there have been -- would there have been a substantial difference in positions as of the 23rd of October, which is not indicated on the map? Would the positions have been much different from those that are indicated? Do you understand my question now?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. On the 23rd and 24th of October, there was an action, a phase of the operation when Kupari was raided and Zupa Dubrovacka was taken. That could not be seen on this map. So these battalions we saw on the map just now reached this area on the 24th, 25th, and 26th. Before that they were a bit further away and they were deployed in a somewhat different fashion at the time when the brigade was commanded by the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So do I take it to mean that the positions for the 23rd are approximate to the positions of the 24th, for our purposes?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Admiral.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Looking at what is in front of you, an order addressed and in the Serbo-Croatian version I'd like to point out a couple of typos so that the Bench can correct them. Yes, but the typos are in translation, unfortunately. It is addressed to the command of the 2nd Operational Group. Is that correct, Admiral? Command of the 2OG?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was compiled by the 2nd Operational Group, their command, that is, and it was sent to my command and to the 472nd Brigade. It is signed by General Pavle Strugar or, rather, Filipovic signed it on his behalf.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The -- the correction I'm referring to is that it should say -- it's from the 2OG but I believe in the English version it only says 2, and it should have command 2OG. And if the Court would be good enough to make that correction. What is the essence of this order? What is it discussing?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order has to do with what I talked about a short while ago, operations of the 472nd Brigade and the 9th VPS. Through those operations, these units came to the position that we saw on the map a short while ago, so this is before the 23rd and the 24th of October. Tasks are given to the units of the 472nd Brigade according to battalions, which positions they are supposed to take, that is. And it can be seen from the order that the command of the 2nd Operational Group is directly assigning tasks to my sector and the brigade, each and every battalion of the brigade separately.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Is there an attachment? Do you see what is an attachment to this particular document? And I will again point out in a moment some corrections that need to be made in the English version, but if you see afterward there is a -- an attachment which is -- which bears at the bottom the name of the artillery Chief of Staff for the 2nd Operational Group, Lieutenant Bozidar Petkovski. Do you see it, Admiral?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is a proposal for engaging artillery in this operation for all of the artillery forces both of the brigade and the 9th Sector. So this document shows that the chief of artillery of the 2nd Operational Group gave detailed tasks to all batteries, all artillery units in this operation. So he said what the targets were and the security zones and the structure of artillery fire and all other details. This is not done usually. However, this is the only operation where the units that bordered on each other had to act in concert and, therefore, the command has to control all artillery units in order to have coordinated action vis-a-vis the targets.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, on the first page of the document which is the one bearing General Strugar's name, there is a section under the -- it says 472nd Motorised Brigade, and the -- I want to just confirm with you that where it says: "To carry out smaller --" the translation is "dislocations of units before dawn and in the following manner," and then it refers to a unit. In Serbo-Croatian, what unit is referred to by 2MTB? Do you see where it says 2MTB under 472nd?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it is the 3rd Battalion that is referred to here and getting the soldier who was from the 3rd Battalion who got killed out. So it's not the 2nd battalion. It's the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What I'm asking you just to assist us with it says I believe in your language 2MTB and should MTB be battalion or brigade? What should be the correct translation, please?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the 2nd MTB, the 2nd Motorised Battalion, not brigade, not brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I believe the English says Your Honour the 2nd Motorised Brigade and I ask if you could please correct it. And I believe that the same occurs in the paragraph indicating the 4th Motorised it should read "Brigade," and it says -- I'm sorry, it should read "Battalion" and it says "Brigade."

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you for your help.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me. I'm just checking something. When -- if and when an artillery chief submits an order or proposal, excuse me, is it done so at the direction of his commander, commander of the Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask this document be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be document Prosecution Exhibit P121.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Looking again at what has been what I believe -- yes, it was admitted in evidence at tab 19. Just taking a look at tab 19, which was P119. Looking back at it, Admiral, this order is an order from Major General Pavle Strugar giving very detailed -- detailed instructions about actions to take place in operations against enemy forces, having specific instructions for the command of the 9th VPS, which is your command, and the 472nd Motorised Brigade to report directly or personally to General Strugar concerning actions taken. Was this --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an order issued on the 24th of October. This is a decision related to further activities, and the order is to the commander of the brigade and the commander of the sector to report to his command post in order to resubordinate the brigade to the 9th Sector. This combat order shows that the units of the sector and the brigade had got to the rock above Zupa, above Kupari and that they took the road between Trebinje and Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, does this order suggest that the operation is clearly under the control and directed by General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: There's one -- there's one aspect of the order that I wish to ask you about, and -- let me just find it. The last page of it, in English, Your Honours, it would be 03409154, there is a paragraph which states: "By using the disciplinary and criminal measures, you should stop the defeatism, betrayal, cowardice and panic and by emphasising bravery, dedication and heroic deeds you should strengthen the unity and toughness of the soldier collective." Do you know perhaps what underlay inserting such a paragraph in this order?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This shows that there were measures to be taken to raise the combat readiness and morale in the units because there had been occurrences of indiscipline and unsoldierly conduct and so on. The commander deemed this was the most important task. Immediately after giving a combat task he talked about the morale. Usually in these combat orders only the essential things are discussed, but this combat order speaks about nothing else but the morale of the troops and providing security which means that this was the focus. This was what they really needed to direct their attention to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Subsequent to the combat operations of 23, 24, 25 October, did you receive information to the effect that shells from positions under the control of the 2nd Operational Group had impacted in the Old Town of Dubrovnik? Did you receive information that there had been shells impacting?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have any such information at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: We're talking about the time period after the actual operations.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Personally, I had heard about that, but it was only after the visit of the journalists and ambassadors, but I learned more about this when the journalists came to Dubrovnik on the 30th of October. It's possible that this was published in the press and in the media, but at the time I knew nothing about it, nor was this in any of our reports, the reports that we received. Those were actually the five or six shells that landed on the Old Town as it turned out later.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are you aware that General Kadijevic on or about the 26th of October wrote to letter to Lord Carrington in which he denied any shelling of the Old Town prior to that date?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the 26th of October. That's when the letter was dated, and it spoke about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Were you required to meet a delegation of ambassadors in Tivat on or about the 29th of October?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: At the meeting, in a similar vein to General Kadijevic, did you inform the ambassadors that the Old Town had not been shelled?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I heard this information after they had returned from their visit to the town itself. However, as I had no facts about that, I told them that I was not familiar and that I was not aware of all these things, which was the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was your comment about -- did you have -- sorry. I -- I withdraw that question. Did you supply the ambassadors with a means of -- of transportation to visit Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I gave them a ship.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And they used this ship to get there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And was there a particular reason why they used a ship as opposed to any other means of transportation?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prior to that, on the 28th of November -- or October, rather, I'm sorry, on the 28th of October, we had negotiations, commander of the 2nd Operational Group, General Strugar had negotiations in Meljine. I think that was the representative, the envoy of the European Commission, Bandioli, he was present and we spoke about this group of ambassadors and how they would reach the town of Dubrovnik. Having in mind the fact that our communication between Boka Kotorska through Herzegovina into Dubrovnik was dangerous in some of its sections, some of the sections of the road were mined and there was not enough time to remove all the mines, and bearing in mind the fact that along the road there were quite many houses that had been burnt down or demolished, General Strugar and I agreed that the safest thing for the ambassadors would be to travel by sea.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: After the ambassadors returned from Dubrovnik -- excuse me, I have to check whether I have the date correct on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: After your meeting on the 29th of October, did you have a social evening with the group of ambassadors?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had dinner at the JNA centre in Tivat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you happen to recall if at some stage during this visit General Strugar also met with the ambassadors?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. General Strugar was not with the ambassadors on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You do not recall his being there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I remember clearly the meeting and everything about it, but this was not envisaged. I received orders to -- to carry out this task. He was probably back at his command post or in Podgorica. I can't remember right now, but I was assigned to carry out that specific task.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: But you don't know for sure if General Strugar may have at some point met with them? You didn't know where he was?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It seems it's a proposition to be quite the contrary of the evidence that was given.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll move on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was there, within 2nd Operational Group, any perceptible attitude, complaints or protest that is were lodged against the 2nd Operational Group by either the European Community or the other side?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in general or on that specific occasion? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: After that time in particular -- well, we're looking at the period from 23 to 25 October. Was there any particular attitude that you might have perceived?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, there was no specific attitude about each protest by the Crisis Staff of Dubrovnik or the representatives of the European Community on our part. There were quite a number of those, and some are reflected in documents in which we were due to reply to those protests. Sometimes we wrote back to the General Staff and to Admiral Brovet specifically. I can't generalise about all the cases, but the general belief was that their side was blowing these instances of shelling out of all proportion and these acts of provocation by firing in general. As far as I remember, on one occasion we asked that the representatives of the European Community come over to our side, that there be delegates who would then tour our units in order to harmonise their positions. They suspected that the Dubrovnik Crisis Staff was exaggerating the extent of shelling and acts of provocation, but we also believed that the European Community tended to often side with Dubrovnik. It was promised to us that there would be delegates who would come over to our side, but this never materialised. I accept, however, that it was possible that there were denials, that we were to blame for many of the cases, many of the things that occurred as part of those acts of provocation by firing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just one clarification in relation to the interpretation on page 72, line 24. It says "they"

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: when actually the admiral said "we suspected that the Dubrovnik Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: After the incident -- excuse me. Once -- once information had made its way to the 2nd Operational Group about a suggestion or indication of impacts in the Old Town and the shelling incident, was any investigation or inquiry undertaken concerning the shelling incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection. Nothing so far in this witness's testimony could possibly be used as a foundation for this question. First of all, we should ask was there any information? Was any information received, followed by the next which, was there any reaction to this information being received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, we have heard that the admiral learnt of some shells falling, five or six he said, in the period before the 30th of October. He heard of them on the 30th of October. I don't know whether that is what you're referring to, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It would qualify as notice, and I would just like -- I think that the question, therefore, would be appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, if I need to repeat it for you, was any investigation or inquiry conduct -- sorry, conducted following the allegations of shelling on the 23rd and 24th of October by forces of the -- of the JNA or the 2nd Operational Group into the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there seems to be a problem with us understanding each other here. The admiral said that he only learned about some things later. My learned friend and colleague, based on this testimony today, draws, on the basis of that, a conclusion which she then links with the 2nd Operational Group. That's the essence of our problem. Admiral is the commander of the 9th VPS. Therefore, I seem to be missing a link between the unit he commands and whoever else may be there. However, the link has not been established for this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: My note, Mr. Petrovic, is that on the 30th of October, from the journalists, the admiral learned that five or six shells had landed in the Old Town, and he said that these had been from units of the 2nd Operational Group. That's my note of the evidence. So that his knowledge on that evidence was not just of his own immediate command but of conduct involving troops of the Operational Group of which he was a part, and the question, as I understand it, is whether there was any inquiry or investigation undertaken into that or shelling incident or those shelling incidents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, that is the question His Honour has just repeated. Are you able to answer it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As for that particular event, as I said, I only learned about that from the journalists. My ship, the 137 patrol boat, was used to transport those journalists, to take them to the town, and after their tour of the town they were returned, driven back to Cavtat. It was then that I heard about it. It was either from Zec or from the boat commander that a lot of damage had occurred in the New Town, in Babin Kuk and Lapad where the hotels are and there was only minor damage in the Old Town, that an old museum called Rupe, an old granary had been damaged but that no one was wounded or killed and that there were only five or six shells that landed there. That's what I learned, I believe, on the 30th or the 31st.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can you indicate whether in the area around Dubrovnik there were any formations that did not belong to the 2nd Operational Group, any formations of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no such formations. All those formations were under the command of the 2nd Operational Group, including of course the 9th Sector which is part of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I don't believe that I was able to -- perhaps we didn't get an answer to the question about inquiry or investigation of the alleged shelling. Are you able to answer that, Admiral?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that there was any investigation, but if I understand you correctly, which position did the command take whenever information was received about shelling at, provocation of firing against the enemy. The procedure that was followed was, roughly speaking, as follows: The commander of the Operational Group, based on an assessment made by his own staff most probably, the assessment was made as to which units may have taken part in such an operation. Then there is an order usually by phone to investigate the case and to report. This is exactly what I did in cases where such things happened under my command. However, an investigation would imply a more thorough procedure. I know what an investigation is supposed to mean, and I was not aware that any investigation was undertaken.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Even in the face of allegations of shelling from units of the 2nd Operational Group, are you aware of any extra measures that may have been taken by the Operational Group to ensure the safety of the Old Town in the face of such an allegation? Was anything done in the way of -- well, was anything done?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any particular measures, but certainly the next combat order the measure was for the commander to repeat the ban on firing on the Old Town and to emphasise the ban on firing on the Old Town, and this was done on a regular basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time, then, Ms. Somers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes. I -- I would say so if -- unless the Chamber wishes to get one more document in on this area. Okay, give up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We would just lose too much critical time. It's important we finish on time for movements of different people.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn until tomorrow morning. I must ask you to return then, Admiral, if you will. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
